text:
The concept is titled "The Chorus of Choice." This production reimagines Sophocles’ *Oedipus Rex* not as a passive viewing experience, but as a participatory ritual. The stage is a circular, multi-level structure representing Thebes, with no traditional proscenium arch. The audience enters as citizens of the city, wearing simple tunics and receiving a "vote token" upon entry.

Instead of a single protagonist, the role of Oedipus is shared among three actors who rotate throughout the performance, each embodying a different aspect of the tragic hero: the ruler, the seeker, and the blind man. The dramatic monologues remain intact in their classical iambic rhythm and thematic depth, exploring fate, hubris, and truth. However, the narrative branches based on audience interaction. At key decision points—such as whether to believe Tiresias or Creon—the audience members use their tokens to vote on the direction of the inquiry. These votes are tallied by a digital chorus that projects the collective will onto the walls, influencing which actor takes the lead and which path of investigation is pursued.

The immersive element extends to the set design, where audience members are occasionally pulled into the scene as minor characters (messengers, guards, or priests), forced to make moral choices that affect the protagonist’s isolation. The climax is not a single revelation but a collective confrontation, where the audience’s accumulated choices determine whether Oedipus finds truth in exile or destruction in power. This fusion preserves the emotional weight and linguistic beauty of Greek tragedy while leveraging modern immersive techniques to make the audience complicit in the tragedy, thereby deepening the thematic resonance of free will versus destiny.
